text:
### Observed differences

- The order of a recurring segment reversed. Earlier, A35, A36 and A41 ran before A26 and A27 in about 97–99 of every 100 traces (the two groups co-occurred in every trace); in the later window, A26 and A27 ran before A35, A36 and A41 in about 97–98 of every 100 traces. [REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015]
- The connections around this segment were rewired. Earlier, A25's outgoing transitions went to A35 (about 38 in 100), A36 (about 31) and A41 (about 27), and A26 led almost exclusively to A30 (about 99 in 100, immediately afterwards). In the later window, A25 leads almost exclusively to A27 (about 96 in 100, typically one step later, whereas A27 previously followed A25 about four steps later in about 92 of 100 cases); A26's transitions now go to A35, A36 or A41 (about 35, 32 and 31 in 100); A30 is instead reached from A35, A36 and A41 (about 30–34 in 100 of each of their transitions, versus almost never earlier); and A27 is almost no longer reached from them (about 1 in 100 or fewer, versus about 29–36 in 100 earlier). [DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, LAG002, LAG005]
- A02 became much rarer. It appeared in about 75 of 100 traces earlier versus about 21 of 100 later (mean occurrences per trace 0.81 versus 0.23), and the partner activities A25, A26, A27, A30, A35, A36, A41, A49 and A50, which previously co-occurred with A02 in about 75 of 100 traces (usually before it), now run without A02 in about 79 of 100 traces. [OCC001, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009]
- A02 also lost its routing role. Earlier, about 91 of every 100 of A02's outgoing transitions went to A50; in the later window its transitions spread over many targets, with A50 at about 13 in 100. A49 now sends about 83 of 100 of its transitions to A50 (previously about 26), while transitions to A02 fell from about 72 to about 3 in 100, and A50 typically follows A49 one step later rather than two. [DIR001, DIR011, LAG009]
- A06 and A10 appear in roughly twice as many traces (about 7 versus 19, and about 9 versus 22 in 100); A06's outgoing mix also changed, but its earlier profile rests on only about 12 observed transitions, so that part is weak. [OCC002, OCC003, DIR002]
- A minor shift: A47's transitions to A48 remain dominant but less so (about 97 in 100 earlier, about 81 in 100 later). [DIR010]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that an existing segment was resequenced and rewired, involving A25, A26, A27, A30, A35, A36 and A41: earlier the flow ran from A25 into one of A35/A36/A41, which in turn preceded A26 and A27 and often led on to A27, with A26 immediately followed by A30; in the later window A25 leads directly to A27, A26 leads into A35/A36/A41, and A30 follows after A35/A36/A41, so the fixed order between the groups {A26, A27} and {A35, A36, A41} is reversed. This is shown directly by the relation items, which flip from about 97–99% one order to about 97–98% the other while both groups co-occur in every trace in both windows, and by the consistent successor and distance changes at A25, A26, A35, A36 and A41, each based on about 200 observations per window. The screening context reinforces this: 38 control-flow items qualified against fewer than one expected if nothing had changed, so the volume of qualifying evidence is not what a stable process typically produces. [REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, LAG002, LAG005]

Limitations: the evidence cannot distinguish a rewiring of a single flow from a shift in the mix of two pre-existing case types whose internal orders were always fixed, since both windows show essentially uniform behaviour within themselves; the items also overlap in describing the same traces and are not independent confirmations, and the distance measures use event positions rather than clock time. [REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, LAG002, LAG005]

Other differences: A02 became far rarer and was bypassed — A49 now leads to A50 directly where it previously led to A02, and A02's own transitions no longer concentrate on A50; A06 and A10 appear in roughly twice as many traces. The evidence does not establish how these changes relate to the resequencing above. [OCC001, DIR001, DIR011, LAG009, OCC002, OCC003]
